title: Forget Big Apps. These Tiny Tools Are Making Millions
channel: Chris Koerner on The Koerner Office Podcast

idea.name: Google Maps lead scraper
idea.one_liner: A self-serve tool that turns Google Maps searches into downloadable local-business leads, sold by subscription and credits.
idea.customer: B2B sales teams, cold callers, SDRs and marketing agencies that need local-business lists.
idea.offer: Search Google Maps by business type and area, then download the results as a spreadsheet.
idea.revenue_model: Monthly subscription converted into scraping credits.

key_quotes.quote: So he started with a Google Maps lead scraper.
So you go to his website, you type in gyms in Texas, and then you have a spreadsheet of every gym in Texas, right?
He used, I think, an Appify actor, an API on the back end to do all the scraping, and he just vibecoded it into a nice, clean little website with a Stripe integration.
So people liked that because a lot of us have subscription fatigue.
He just kind of told some friends about it in the sales space.

claims.claim: The product costs $35 a month, with the payment converted into credits.
claims.quote: Charges 35 bucks a month, but he allowed customers to convert that 35 bucks into credits.

claims.claim: Unused credits remain available for nine months after cancellation.
claims.quote: So if they canceled their account, they could still come back 9 months later and use the rest of their credits to scrape more.

claims.claim: After about seven months, the business had $3,500 in monthly recurring revenue.
claims.quote: So he's been doing this for like 7 months and he's doing 3500 bucks in monthly recurring revenue.

claims.claim: The business's costs were almost zero.
claims.quote: His costs are almost zero. His customer support is basically zero.

claims.claim: Customer support was nearly zero.
claims.quote: His customer support is basically zero. It's a self-s served product and yeah, this is a guy who had no tech experience and he's doing well and is growing double digits every month.

claims.claim: Revenue was growing by double digits each month.
claims.quote: It's a self-s served product and yeah, this is a guy who had no tech experience and he's doing well and is growing double digits every month.

claims.claim: The host projects possible future monthly revenue of $5,000, $10,000, or $20,000 to $30,000.
claims.quote: His 3500 MR today eventually will be 5,000 and 10,000, maybe 20 or 30,000.

acquisition_channels.details: Nico told friends in the sales space; the host says word of mouth drove early use.

ideas.delivery: Nico runs a self-serve website that queries Google Maps through an Apify actor and returns a spreadsheet; Stripe handles payment. A technical friend helps with technical work.
ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR may apply to identifiable business contact data; PECR applies to downstream marketing. DMCC Act subscription rules may be relevant to the recurring plan.

idea.one_liner: A tool that summarizes a competitor's Amazon reviews into customer feedback and product-improvement insights for DTC brands.
idea.customer: Shopify brands and independent Amazon sellers.
idea.offer: Paste an Amazon product URL and receive a report of compliments, complaints, phrases and suggested improvements.
